content.en:
• Prime Number: Natural number greater than 1 with exactly two distinct factors: 1 and itself.
• Smallest & Only Even Prime: 2.
• 1 is neither prime nor composite.
• Prime Distribution: Exactly 25 primes between 1 and 100; 15 primes between 1 and 50.
• 6k ± 1 Rule: All prime numbers greater than 3 can be expressed in the form 6k + 1 or 6k - 1 (converse is not necessarily true).
• Coprimes (Relatively Prime): Two numbers having an HCF of exactly 1. They need not be prime themselves (e.g., 8 and 9 are coprime).
• Primality Test: To test if N is prime, test divisibility by primes less than or equal to √N.

content.en:
Illustrative Problem: Is 197 a prime number?
Solution: √197 ≈ 14. Primes ≤ 14 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13. Testing divisibility: 197 is not divisible by 2, 3, 5, 7 (197/7=28 r 1), 11 (197/11=17 r 10), or 13 (197/13=15 r 2). Since none divides 197, 197 is prime.

question.en: How many prime numbers exist such that their square when divided by 24 leaves a remainder of 1?
question.hi: How many prime numbers exist such that their square when divided by 24 leaves a remainder of 1?

explanation.en: Any prime p > 3 can be written as 6k ± 1. Then p² = (6k ± 1)² = 36k² ± 12k + 1 = 12k(3k ± 1) + 1. Since k and (3k ± 1) must have opposite parities, one of them is even, making the product 12 * (even) a multiple of 24. Thus, p² = 24m + 1. Hence, the square of EVERY prime number greater than 3 leaves remainder 1 when divided by 24. There are infinitely many such primes.
